entries.observed_reference: Terrain3D.blur builds a 1-D Gaussian kernel then returns H.clone(), E.clone() without convolving.
entries.v1_behavior: Real separable Gaussian blur (kernel_size=max(3,int(6*sigma)|1), normalized, replicate boundary) applied to H and E before pour.
entries.rationale: The reference intent (docstring, kernel construction, consolidation §7.4) is a blur; the no-op is a defect.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/terrain.rs: asymmetric impulse spreads under blur; constant field unchanged; no-op implementation fails.

entries.observed_reference: MemoryCenters.write calls compute_rbf_weights without sigma, so sigma_read is used for write candidates; sigma_write is never used.
entries.v1_behavior: Executed reference behavior kept: write candidates use sigma_read. sigma_write retained in config and documented unused.
entries.rationale: new_center_threshold values were tuned against the executed width; switching widths changes admission rates without evidence.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/center_write.rs asserts the write path uses sigma_read (a sigma_write mutant changes the created/reinforced decision on a fixture).

entries.observed_reference: _recall_impl calls read_compound_records without terrain_queries; terrain part is zeros.
entries.v1_behavior: Same: terrain part contributes 0 to text recall; profile exposes terrain_read_influence=none.
entries.rationale: No tested terrain-aware read policy exists; do not advertise one.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/center_read.rs: compound read with terrain None equals semantic+context only.

entries.observed_reference: TextMemory.recall merges LTM/STM matches by key_text keeping the higher weight.
entries.v1_behavior: Distinct records stay distinct; merge across layers only by RecordId; both layers reported.
entries.rationale: Key-text dedup hides contradictory records and provenance.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/record_recall.rs: two records with the same key text and different values both appear.

entries.observed_reference: read/read_compound increment usage by default; recall increments read_count.
entries.v1_behavior: Reads never mutate. Feedback is the only usage/learning-from-use path.
entries.rationale: Host Recall/Search/Inspect must be side-effect free and idempotent.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/center_read.rs: repeated reads leave state digest unchanged; runtime engine tests: commit seq unchanged after recall.

entries.observed_reference: _load_impl catches exceptions and logs; memory continues empty.
entries.v1_behavior: Corrupt/incompatible state fails closed; fresh-empty only via explicit create.
entries.rationale: Silent empty state is data loss presented as health.
entries.discriminating_test: runtime tests/store.rs corrupt-open returns Corrupt, never Ready.

entries.observed_reference: State records fatigue but not steps_since_consolidation.
entries.v1_behavior: Full scheduler state persisted (fatigue, steps_since_consolidation, tick, epoch, seq).
entries.rationale: Restart must not shift sleep boundaries.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/dynamics.rs split-run equals uninterrupted run; runtime store round-trip.

entries.observed_reference: to_ltm_key (384→64) and stm_to_ltm U (16→64) are independently initialized; consolidated LTM keys are not aligned with direct LTM query projections.
entries.v1_behavior: Each record/center retains its canonical LTM key computed at observe time; consolidation writes that key. U kept for reference fixtures only.
entries.rationale: Without alignment LTM-only recall of consolidated memories is chance-level.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/consolidation.rs: store→consolidate→mask STM→recall finds the record; the U-based mutant fails.

entries.observed_reference: splat indexes H[x,y,z] with position[0]→dim0 while grid_sample reads position[0] along the last tensor dim.
entries.v1_behavior: One convention: position component i ↔ grid axis i for splat and sample; index (x*G+y)*G+z.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/terrain.rs: sample after asymmetric splat peaks at the splat position; swapped-axis mutant fails.

execution_evidence.conclusion: Splat position[i] indexes tensor axis i; grid_sample position[0] reads the last tensor axis. Reference sample returns H[z,y,x].

entries.observed_reference: store() updates fatigue with 0.1*intensity and may auto-consolidate; homeostasis step() is caller-driven and separate.
entries.v1_behavior: One learning tick per unique committed Observe: write → splat → fatigue/scheduler → homeostasis (both layers, both terrains). Reads/duplicates advance nothing. Maintenance{advance:n≤10000}.
entries.rationale: The host has no separate step caller; an explicit frozen schedule is required.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/dynamics.rs; runtime engine tests: duplicate observe leaves tick/fatigue unchanged.

entries.observed_reference: Adapter namespace hashes agent_session_id and resolved_scope_digest.
entries.v1_behavior: Unchanged. Cross-session reuse only through host-authorized replay/share (task 024).

entries.observed_reference: merge_similar binds h_i and h_j as tensor views, then assigns total_h to self.h[idx_i] before computing weighted K/V/e. h_i therefore becomes total_h in subsequent arithmetic. For h_i=2,h_j=3,V_i=1,V_j=4, the executed V_i is 3.4000000953674316 rather than the nonaliased weighted average 2.8.
entries.v1_behavior: Corrected: merge uses the PRE-merge intensities h_i, h_j for the weighted K/V/e/ltm_key average, i.e. V_i' = (h_i·V_i + h_j·V_j)/(h_i+h_j+1e-8); the executed reference value (aliased h_i = total_h) is preserved only in the oracle fixture as expected-difference data.
entries.rationale: The aliasing is a Python view side effect, not an intended rule; the docstring and spec describe an intensity-weighted average.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/consolidation.rs: explicit h=[2,3], V=[1,4] merge yields 2.8 (aliased mutant would yield 3.4).

entries.observed_reference: torch.topk returns ties in an unspecified, non-ascending index order.
entries.v1_behavior: Rust top-k resolves exact ties by ascending center index (contract §4). Oracle comparisons treat tied candidates as an equivalence group: indices must match as sets within each tie group and weights must match elementwise after sorting by index.
entries.rationale: Deterministic, documented tie policy; reference order is not reproducible.
entries.discriminating_test: core tests/numeric.rs tie stability; fixture loaders compare tie groups.
